title: 2D Adaptive trochoidal: slots to a wall instead of walking the contour, and no outside start

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What happens

The 2D Adaptive strategy does not adapt to the free space. With trochoidal passes it walks the path in the wrong way:

- It makes straight slots until the tool reaches a wall. The slot is at the full width of the tool.
- It does not walk the selected edge with trochoidal moves.
- It cannot start from the outside of the part.

The maintainer reported this while cutting a part with the 2D Adaptive strategy.

## What is expected

- The trochoidal pass follows the selected contour, like a spiral along the edge, with small trochoidal loops.
- The step and the loop width adapt to the space that is free at each point.
- The operation can start from the outside of the stock.

## Why it matters

- The full-width slots load the tool. The strategy exists to keep the engagement small.
- The current path is slow, and it does not cut the shape that the user selected.
- Without an outside start, the entry is inefficient on an open edge.

## What to check

- The engagement limit: the loop width and the step must come from it at each point, not only at the first pass.
- The pass layout of the adaptive strategy: does it fall back to slotting when the island or the wall is near?
- The start side: the strategy must accept an Outside start on an open edge.
- The pins: `adaptive_troch_*` and the example catalog cases may not cover an open edge with a near wall.

## Missing at filing

- The sketch, the tool, the stock and the posted program. Add them as a comment when the case is reproduced.

If any of these slots can gouge the part or the fixture, this issue is `P1`. Confirm on the fixture first.
